title: What is AWS, and what is the difference between a Region, an Availability Zone (AZ), and an Edge Location?
shortTitle: AWS, Region, Availability Zone and Edge Location
keyPoints: AWS is a cloud computing platform that rents servers, storage, databases, and managed services on demand with pay-per-use billing.
A Region is an isolated geographic area such as Mumbai (ap-south-1) containing multiple data-center clusters for data sovereignty and fault isolation.
An Availability Zone is one or more physically separate data centers inside a Region with independent power, cooling, and networking.
Every Region has at least three Availability Zones connected by low-latency links so you can build highly available applications.
An Edge Location is a small CloudFront CDN point of presence placed near end users to cache content and reduce latency.
Choose a Region based on latency to users, regulatory compliance such as RBI data residency, service availability, and pricing.
AZ names like ap-south-1a are randomized per account; use AZ IDs like aps1-az1 for stable cross-account references.

s1_definition.oneliner: Region is the city, Availability Zone is a separate building in that city, and Edge Location is a tiny kiosk near the customer for speed.
s1_definition.profdef:
- **AWS (Amazon Web Services)** – A cloud computing platform that provides on-demand servers, storage, databases, networking, and managed services, all billed by usage instead of upfront hardware purchase.
- **Region** – A separate geographic area such as Mumbai (`ap-south-1`) containing multiple isolated data-center clusters, chosen for latency and compliance.
- **Availability Zone (AZ)** – One or more physically separate data centers inside a Region with independent power, cooling, and networking, connected to other AZs by low-latency links.
- **Edge Location** – A small CloudFront CDN presence point placed close to end users to cache content and terminate connections with minimal latency.
- **Data Sovereignty** – Data stays inside a Region unless explicitly copied, which matters for regulatory requirements like RBI data-residency rules in India.
s1_definition.analogy: Think of National Bank of India. AWS is the whole banking network. A Region is a city like Mumbai where the bank has operations. An Availability Zone is an individual branch building in that city with its own power supply and security – if one branch has a power failure, the other branches in the same city keep working. An Edge Location is a small ATM kiosk placed in a shopping mall close to where Rajesh lives, so he gets cash quickly without travelling to the main branch.

sections.s6_takeaway:
AWS is Amazon's cloud platform where you rent computing, storage, networking, and managed services on demand and pay only for what you use, instead of buying and running your own data centers. The three terms that confuse people – Region, Availability Zone, and Edge Location – sit at three different levels of scale. A Region is a geographic area like Mumbai, identified as ap-south-1, and it is isolated from other Regions, which matters for banking because RBI requires Indian customer data to stay inside India, so we deploy to the Mumbai Region and the data never leaves it unless we explicitly copy it.

An Availability Zone is one or more physically separate data centers inside a Region, each with its own independent power, cooling, and network. A Region has at least three of them. We spread our application across Availability Zones so that if one data center loses power, the instances in the other zones keep serving customers with no downtime. In practice we put subnets in different zones and let the load balancer span them, which is how we achieve high availability within a single Region.

An Edge Location is part of the CloudFront content delivery network – a small point of presence placed physically close to end users. It caches content like statement PDFs and web assets so the first byte reaches the customer in a few milliseconds, and it offloads traffic from the Region. There are far more Edge Locations than Regions because their whole purpose is to be near the customer.

At National Bank of India we used exactly this layering. Our statement service runs across three Availability Zones in the Mumbai Region for resilience, the PDFs are stored in an S3 bucket in that same Region for compliance, and CloudFront Edge Locations serve the downloads fast to customers all over India. One senior detail is that Availability Zone names are randomized per account, so ap-south-1a in my account may be a different physical building than in yours, which is why AWS also exposes a stable Availability Zone ID when you need to coordinate placement across accounts.

Remember one sentence: A Region is the city you choose for compliance, Availability Zones are separate buildings in that city you spread across for resilience, and Edge Locations are ATM kiosks near users for speed.
